background: Danske Bank is Denmark's largest bank, a Nordic universal bank funded by Danish and Nordic deposits and covered bonds, lending to households and companies across Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland, with the Estonian money-laundering case behind it.
synthesis: Rated AA- on average across all three, the weakest of them at A+, one on a positive outlook and two on a stable outlook, after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026, the bank's credit standing has improved markedly. CET1 of 17.0% is above the median for EU and Nordic banks, but leverage of 4.4% is in the bottom quarter, and liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 162% above the median and NSFR of 122% just below it. The ratios are drifting down: since 30 Jun 2025 CET1 has fallen 1.6 points, leverage 0.4 points and LCR 18 points, while NSFR has been broadly flat. The newest flagged item, on 26 Aug 2026, is a move to a positive outlook by one of the three.
